prompt.brief: Design a service where users watch products across marketplaces and receive one timely notification when a price rule is met, despite stale data, provider limits, retries, and traffic spikes.
successSignals: Separate price collection freshness from alert evaluation and notification delivery.
Make marketplace throttling, retries, and adaptive polling explicit.
Use durable state and idempotency so at-least-once events do not spam users.
Define what a price means when variants, sellers, currencies, shipping, or taxes differ.

functional: Create, pause, resume, and delete alerts for a product or offer.
Support target-price, percentage-drop, and back-in-stock rules with a cooldown.
Collect prices from multiple providers and show current price plus history.
Notify through user-selected channels and expose delivery status.
Allow users to unsubscribe, change cadence, and export or delete their data.
nonFunctional: Deliver a triggered alert within 1 minute after a qualifying observation is accepted.
Never lose a committed alert or price observation; duplicate notifications are unacceptable.
Respect provider rate limits, robots/terms constraints, user quotas, and notification opt-outs.
Tolerate provider outages and stale prices without presenting stale data as current.
Keep alert CRUD responsive even while collection and delivery backlogs grow.
scaleAssumptions: 10 million registered users, 2 million daily active users, and 50 million active alerts.
100 million product observations per day across providers, with a 10x burst during sales.
A product is collected every 15 minutes by default; hot products can receive shorter cadences within quota.
Assume 5% of observations qualify for evaluation and 1% result in a notification after cooldowns.

metrics.label: Observation rate
metrics.description: 100M daily observations; provision collectors and queues for ~12K/s bursts.

metrics.label: Active rules
metrics.description: Rules drive indexed evaluation lookups; do not scan every user on each price event.

metrics.label: Notification rate
metrics.description: At 1% of observations, with campaign spikes and provider-specific quotas.

metrics.label: Freshness target
metrics.description: Default product freshness; show observed_at and provider status with every price.

entities.notes: Normalized offer identity across provider and seller dimensions.

entities.name: AlertRule
entities.notes: Indexed user rule evaluated against accepted observations.

entities.name: PriceObservation

entities.name: NotificationLedger
entities.notes: Idempotent delivery record for one alert transition.

apis.contract: { productId, condition, threshold, channels, cooldown } -> { ruleId, status }
apis.notes: Normalize the offer, validate thresholds and consent, then write the rule idempotently.
Return the latest accepted observation with currency/offer semantics.

apis.contract: { threshold?, cadence?, channels?, status? } -> updated rule
apis.notes: Authorize the owner and version the rule for in-flight evaluation.

apis.contract: { offer, price, observedAt, sourceVersion, requestId } -> { accepted, eventId }
apis.notes: Authenticate provider adapters, reject late/malformed data, and deduplicate requestId.

dataFlow.title: Create the alert
dataFlow.description: The API validates the rule, resolves product and offer identity, stores preferences, and returns without waiting for a provider fetch.

dataFlow.title: Schedule collection
dataFlow.description: A scheduler chooses due offers from cadence, demand, freshness, provider quota, and exponential backoff, then dispatches bounded jobs.

dataFlow.title: Accept a price observation
dataFlow.description: Adapters normalize currency, variant, seller, shipping, and availability; late observations are rejected or marked and durable price events are published.

dataFlow.title: Evaluate the rule
dataFlow.description: The evaluator loads only active rules for the offer, compares the previous accepted state, applies cooldowns, and writes one notification decision.

dataFlow.title: Deliver asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Channel workers retry provider delivery, record attempts in the ledger, and expose opt-out or failure status without blocking collection.

architecture.title: Price alert reference architecture
architecture.summary: A scheduled collection pipeline turns marketplace prices into durable events; a stateful evaluator deduplicates transitions before notification delivery.

layers.label: Experience and control plane
layers.description: Clients manage products, alert rules, channels, and delivery preferences.

layers.label: Collection and event plane
layers.description: Schedulers and workers fetch current prices with provider-aware throttling.

layers.label: Evaluation and delivery plane
layers.description: Rules are evaluated against price changes and delivered with retry and idempotency controls.

keyPaths.description: Client → gateway → alert service → durable catalog store.

keyPaths.label: Price evaluation path

deepDives.title: Provider freshness and adaptive polling
points: For the multi-marketplace price-alert service, one qualifying price transition produces at most one notification per rule/cooldown window.
Design for the failure case where provider throttling, stale variants, late observations, and retries must not spam users or show false prices; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Offer identity and rule evaluation
points: For the multi-marketplace price-alert service, one qualifying price transition produces at most one notification per rule/cooldown window.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by the multi-marketplace price-alert service access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Cooldowns and notification idempotency
points: For the multi-marketplace price-alert service, one qualifying price transition produces at most one notification per rule/cooldown window.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by the multi-marketplace price-alert service access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

tradeoffs.title: Polling freshness versus provider limits
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use demand-aware cadence, provider quotas, adaptive backoff, and explicit stale indicators.
tradeoffs.caution: Polling every alert uniformly overloads providers and still cannot guarantee fresh data.

tradeoffs.title: Observed price versus landed price
tradeoffs.recommendation: Model price, shipping, tax, currency, seller, and variant explicitly and let users choose comparison semantics.
tradeoffs.caution: Comparing only sticker price produces misleading alerts across marketplaces.

tradeoffs.title: Immediate notification versus cooldown
tradeoffs.recommendation: Emit on a rule transition with a cooldown and a durable notification ledger.
tradeoffs.caution: Notifying on every observation creates alert fatigue and duplicate delivery.

commonMistakes: Scanning every user rule for every provider observation.
Overwriting a newer observation with a late response.
Ignoring seller, variant, currency, shipping, or tax dimensions.
Retrying notifications without a dedupe key and cooldown.
Showing stale provider data as current.

followUps.question: What if a provider is throttling?
followUps.answer: Use a quota-aware scheduler, exponential backoff, cached last observation with freshness, and lower-priority collection for cold offers.

followUps.question: What if price drops and rises during retries?
followUps.answer: Order observations by provider timestamp/source version, evaluate transitions from accepted state, and keep each notification decision idempotent.

followUps.question: How do you handle unsubscribe during delivery?
followUps.answer: Recheck consent before sending, record the skipped attempt, and prevent future intents from using the revoked channel.

rubric.description: The answer defines provider-aware collection, normalized offers, freshness, indexed rule evaluation, cooldowns, and idempotent notification delivery, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make the multi-marketplace price-alert service state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the multi-marketplace price-alert service consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
